# Microwave: design, implementation, physical validation, review

This is a force-tested **provisional real-to-sim mechanism**, built on the existing `microwave_body` asset. It is not hardware-calibrated. The camera evidence establishes appearance and approximate geometry; no observed microwave opening, load-cell measurements, door weight, or exact model label is available. Consequently the force targets and hidden mechanism are stated engineering priors. All reported motion results are offline MuJoCo simulation, not online reconstruction performance or measured appliance behavior.

## Evidence and real-world scale

The source asset is `../../assets/small_appliances/microwave_body` (`model.json`, `model.blend`, `parts/*.obj`, `collision/*.obj`, `build.py`, `notes.md`). Its stainless trim, smoked window, enamel shell, photo-derived keypad, separate button and turntable are retained. `evidence/provenance.json` records source hashes; `mjcf/visual_manifest.json` maps 10,050 inherited triangles to 11 material groups. Existing source files are unchanged; the upgraded simulation and collision model live here.

Inspected source crops f0299 and f0321 show Panasonic branding, a door ending at the control-panel seam, no projecting handle, and a large release button at the bottom right. They support the left-hinge interpretation in the constrained articulation, but do not expose the hinge pin or internal latch. No direction or spring trajectory was measured from motion.

| Asset frame | X right, −Y front, Z up; support-footprint centre at z=0 | Existing OBJ convention; not GLB's Y-up coordinates |
| Exterior W × D × H | 600 × 436 × 355 mm | Retained mesh envelope; front trim projects beyond shell |
| Structure envelope | 600 × 405 × 340 mm | Supplied layout proxy; excludes some trim/feet |
| Raw f0305 door rectangle | 475.3 × 293.1 mm | Rerun of supplied native-pixel annotation via ktools; 99.8% plane inliers |
| Constrained rectangle | 479.515 × 287.027 mm | Supplied layout fit, not independent of the raw annotation |
| Exterior moving door | approximately 479.5 × 321 mm | Existing visible outer trim; collision W=479 mm |
| Other raw checks | f0299 front 550.3 × 312.3 mm; door 451.5 × 311.8 mm; top 573.7 × 468.6 mm | Existing asset evidence; glossy surfaces, edge selection and pose/depth disagree |
| World placement | [0.830, −1.2375, 0.985] m; yaw 180° | Source asset's instance transform; not baked into standalone MJCF |
| Local hinge | [−0.28572, −0.20778, 0.17146] m, axis [0,0,−1] | Constrained vertical left edge; WORLD hinge [1.11572, −1.02972, 1.15646] m |
| Maximum opening | 100° = 1.745329252 rad | User-requested mechanical prior; replaces unverified 1.9 rad |

The measurement CLI rerun is saved in `evidence/measurement.json`, including actual wall time. It reuses the supplied pixels, so it is a reproducibility check, not a new independent measurement. The reconstruction scale derives from the existing depth-estimated WORLD transform (reported approximately 4% accuracy, unverified). These inconsistent rectangles do not establish millimetric accuracy.

As a product-class comparison, Panasonic's [NN-SN966S owner's manual, printed p.19](https://help.na.panasonic.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/NNSN766_SN966_F0003BR60AP_ENG.pdf) gives W×H×D 606×356×493 mm and approximately 37 lb (16.7 kg); its control diagram labels a door release button and safety lock. The [Panasonic specification table](https://help.na.panasonic.com/answers/features-and-specifications-microwave-oven-model-nn-sn766s-model-nn-sn966s/) lists a 420 mm tray for the large model, but contains an inconsistent model heading. These are comparison products, **not an identification** of the captured microwave. The adopted total is 16.8 kg, rounding the 37 lb conversion. The 57 mm depth discrepancy and much smaller hidden tray are unresolved; replacing the measured scene with that product's dimensions would be unjustified without a model label or depth measurement. The smaller tray is a usable completion, not a claim of exact product fidelity.

`params.py: PARAMS['lengths']` centralizes geometry and all mechanism lengths. `SCALE=1.0` multiplies every mesh, pivot, contact primitive, stroke and inertia length; masses stay fixed and inertia scales as SCALE². Angles remain radians. Changes require rebuilding and retesting: geometry calibration does not automatically identify new spring/friction laws. The final length ledger below is in nominal metres.

## Masses, inertia and materials

| Rigid body | Mass kg | Real-world justification / limitation |
|---|---:|---|
| Fixed housing, equipment, keypad | 13.27 | Residual to 16.8 kg product-class total; includes transformer/inverter, shell, hub and fixed panel |
| Moving door | 2.50 | Assumed composite steel/glass/plastic door, about 15% of total; includes illustrative hooks |
| Door strike pad, rigidly attached | 0.01 | Equivalent compliant strike contact; combined moving door mass 2.51 kg |
| Release pushbar | 0.060 | Assumed 104 mm-wide molded pushbar with thin metal skin; no contents |
| Glass turntable | 0.960 | Ø286×6 mm disk corresponds to approximately 2490 kg/m³ glass; no food load |
| Total | **16.800** | Empty appliance prior, not weighed hardware |

Explicit inertias prevent visual overlaps or convex hulls from inflating mass. The door and button use composite rectangular-envelope inertia, Ixx=m(y²+z²)/12 and cyclic permutations. The table is a solid disk, Izz=mr²/2, Ixx=Iyy=m(3r²+h²)/12. Housing inertia sums the hollow collision pieces with the parallel-axis theorem, normalized to 13.27 kg; corner overlaps are retained as an effective equipment distribution, not claimed sheet-metal density. Housing COM is biased toward the equipment bay. The small pad uses 2mr²/5. Exact COMs, tensors and methods are included below and in `evidence/inertias.json`. Each tensor is positive; the armature is additional reflected inertia, not counted as product mass.

The housing is fixed to WORLD as a **mechanism test fixture**, consistent with the supplied static layout. Its mass/inertia is authored for later free-root integration, but these tests cannot establish whole-appliance slipping/tipping, foot contact, or forces needed to move the appliance. Add a free root and actual support contacts before testing those behaviors.

Visual materials retain the source's photographic keypad and stainless appearance; roughness, metallicity and hidden cavity enamel are assumptions. MuJoCo receives UV-mapped keypad PNG and material-separated surfaces. Blender Cycles provides the material review images; its transparent glass and shading are richer than MuJoCo's raster renderer. The material ledger below states the exported values. No material implies microwave heating, radiation or electrical simulation.

## Native MuJoCo mechanisms

Defaults are `microwave_door_mechanism`, `microwave_button_mechanism`, `microwave_table_mechanism`, `microwave_visual`, and `microwave_collision`. Every authored MJCF object name is prefixed `microwave_`; the explicitly requested keyframe `rest` is the sole named-object exception.

| Parameter | Door hinge | Release slide | Turntable |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Axis | [0,0,−1] | [0,+1,0] into panel | [0,0,+1] |
| Range | 0…1.745329252 rad | 0…0.009 m | Continuous; no limits |
| frictionloss | 0.080 N·m | 0.30 N | 0.001 N·m |
| Viscous damping | 0.22 N·m·s/rad | 10 N·s/m | 0.0005 N·m·s/rad |
| Armature | 0.0005 kg·m² | 0.005 kg effective mass | 0.00001 kg·m² |
| Native joint stiffness | 0 | 650 N/m | 0 |
| Native springref | 0 rad | −0.001 m | 0 rad |
| Extra tendon spring | 2 N·m/rad, deadband [0.35,100] rad | 8000 N/m, deadband [−1,0.007] m | None |

All joint force values are unmeasured engineering assumptions. The door dry friction gives approximately 0.172 N at the 464.72 mm test lever; it permits easy free motion without drift. Damping dissipates opening energy and brings the model to approximately 35°. Door armature is a small hinge hardware allowance, 0.26% of its approximate hinge-axis inertia. The table's small losses represent a free roller/hub bearing, **not an energized gearmotor**, and satisfy the requested low-friction behavior. Button damping suppresses unrealistic inertial release under a low-force step; its 5 g armature approximates coupled release hardware.

Opening torque is τ=2·max(0.35−q,0) over the operating range. The 0.70 N·m closed preload stores 0.1225 J. Once q exceeds 0.35 rad (20.05°), the spring is unloaded: it exerts no reclosing torque at wide angles. Damping/inertia carry the door to its settled pop angle. The remote deadband endpoint at 100 rad is unreachable with the 100° limit; it introduces no spring effect in the usable range. A full-range hinge spring would incorrectly pull the door closed again and is deliberately not used.

Button restoring force magnitude before friction/damping is 650(x+0.001)+8000·max(x−0.007,0) N. Initial preload is 0.65 N; tangent stiffness changes from 650 to 8650 N/m at 7 mm. At x=7.6 mm the spring force is 10.39 N, plus direction/rate-dependent friction and damping. This gives substantial low-resistance travel followed by a sharp second stage. A separate soft joint limit stops travel near 9 mm; the 40 N overload test reaches 9.121 mm. The negative first-spring reference seats the button against its outward stop; finite solver compliance leaves approximately −4.86 μm at rest.

### Hook latch and contact-only adhesion

The images cannot constrain an internal lever's geometry, ratios or interlock motion, so a physically dimensioned **lever contact model is not claimed**. Two illustrative hook meshes are attached to the door. Their contacts are disabled; the actual latch surrogate is `microwave_latch`, a joint equality holding qdoor=0. `controller.py` is required for the discrete release rule, as allowed by the task:

* Before each 0.5 ms step, release equality if button position ≥7.6 mm.
* Relatch only when button ≤1 mm, door ≤0.002 rad (0.115°) and |door speed| ≤0.15 rad/s.
* Otherwise retain the equality's existing state; no qpos/qvel teleport and no timed door motor.

The position is read directly from the joint state corresponding to the named position sensor, avoiding stale sensor data. The latch state is `data.eq_active`, so it belongs to each simulation instance. The hysteresis separates button release/rearm and prevents immediate relatching during a held press. The velocity gate limits energy loss when a closing latch engages. Closing under a force and a second release are tested.

`microwave_seal_adhesion` is a native **adhesion actuator**, gain 1 N, ctrlrange [0,1], `rest.ctrl=1`. Its dedicated welded pad body has only the seal/striker contact; it does not attract every door collision. The [MuJoCo 3.5 actuator reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.5.0/XMLreference.html#actuator-adhesion) defines the body contact transmission. A 50 μm contact-detection margin and equal gap allow stable touching detection; no positive-separation contact repulsion is added. Adhesion is consequently confined to this microscopic detected-contact band and has zero generalized force when separated. Control remains 1 even after the latch releases. No distance-dependent virtual magnet is applied.

The pad is an effective contact attraction prior, not evidence of a real rubber gasket or magnet on this microwave. Its 1 N attraction contributes about 0.452 N·m at rest, below the opening preload after dry friction. Hook retention is mechanical and is not replaced by that weak attraction. There is **no finite nondestructive latched handle-pull breakaway** in the equality surrogate; the 35 N hold test establishes a lower bound, not a structural failure force. The actual unit has no handle: all “handle” tests apply tangential force to the right door edge at the named grasp site. With the opening spring unloaded and equality released in a component bench, pad/hinge pull-off is bracketed at 0.8–1.3 N. Those tests must not be confused with button actuation force or hook strength.

### Collision and solver

Ten convex housing boxes leave the cavity open. A thinner front base and split equipment bay create a genuine empty button pocket; the original broad base and equipment proxy would interfere after 8 mm. A cavity-floor piece matches the visible enamel top at z=36 mm, preventing contents from sinking into the floor. The door is one thin box, button one box, table a convex cylinder. The small seal sphere and striker box use a dedicated explicit pair. Visual meshes have contype=conaffinity=0; they never create convex hulls across the hollow cavity. The scene includes no visual-only hidden latch collision. Fixed-body shell overlaps are intentional union pieces, not penetrations between independently movable bodies.

Parent collision filtering is **disabled** so tests check door/button against the housing instead of silently suppressing parent-child contact. Seal geoms have no automatic masks and interact through their explicit pair only, preventing adhesion on unrelated objects. With the door open, a ray through the chamber reaches the rear at 586 mm from its starting point. A 1057-state door/button grid has no geometric penetration beyond floating-point roundoff.

Contact friction triples (sliding coefficient, torsional length, rolling length), all assumed for dry material pairs: shell [0.4,0.003,0.0001], door/edge [0.6,0.003,0.0001], pad [0.8,0.003,0.0001], button [0.5,0.002,0.0001], glass [0.25,0.001,0.0001]. The explicit pair uses [0.8,0.8,0.003,0.0001,0.0001] for its two sliding directions. Contact dimensionality is 3: sliding terms are active; torsion/rolling values are authored for extensions but inactive at condim=3. These are contact coefficients, not substitutes for joint frictionloss.

Integrator `implicitfast`, Newton solver, elliptic cone, timestep 0.0005 s, 100 maximum iterations, tolerance 1e−10, gravity [0,0,−9.81] m/s². Contact solref [0.002,1] s/damping ratio, solimp [0.95,0.99,0.001]; joint-limit solreflimit [0.003,1], solimplimit [0.95,0.99,0.001]; latch equality solref [0.002,1], solimp [0.999,0.9999,0.001]. Unspecified impedance midpoint/power retain MuJoCo's 0.5/2 defaults. Solimp width is in the corresponding constraint's units (metres or radians). All regularization settings are numerical choices, not material stiffness measurements. Critical damping limits rebound; time constants exceed the 2×dt safety threshold. Solver limits are compliant, not exact kinematic clamps. Joint friction uses native solreffriction [0.02,1] and solimpfriction [0.9,0.95,0.001,0.5,2], verified from the compiled model; these are regularization priors, not hardware data. Energy accounting is enabled.

## Isaac Lab equivalent and limitations

`isaac/actuators.py` targets the documented [Isaac Lab 2.2.1 custom actuator interface](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v2.2.1/_modules/isaaclab/actuators/actuator_base.html), with `MicrowaveActuatorCfg`, `MicrowaveActuator`, and a separately executable batched Torch `MicrowaveLaw`. Use one actuator group selecting all three named joints; the adapter resolves their actual order. Native drives and native friction are zero to avoid double counting. Armatures use the same values as MJCF. Populate native USD joint bounds as above; the turntable must remain continuous.

The law implements the same preload, unilateral opening spring, two-stage button, release/rearm state, viscous losses and per-environment reset. Dry friction is approximated by f·tanh(v/0.0001), with velocity in rad/s or m/s: this is a smooth dynamic approximation and does not reproduce MuJoCo's exact static-friction complementarity. PhysX's load-dependent friction coefficient is not equated to an absolute N/N·m frictionloss.

Its latch uses a 20,000 N·m/rad, 100 N·m·s/rad compliant lock, active only while latched and |q|<0.035 rad (about 2°). It is not an equality and may escape under overload. Explicit limit supplements use 2000 N·m/rad and 20 N·m·s/rad for door, 200,000 N/m and 40 N·s/m for button; these are numerical priors, not matched MuJoCo solref conversions. The force caps are 100 N·m door, 300 N button, 5 N·m table, with configured velocity limit 100 in each joint's SI velocity units. Stiff limits require physics substeps no larger than 0.5 ms and solver validation.

A real seal/striker **contact mask must be supplied every substep** via `set_seal_contact`. Without it, attraction is zero. The 1 N contact force is represented by its closed-door lever torque, an approximation valid in the microscopic seal contact band; no attraction acts just because the door is near closed. The Torch law is unit-tested on CPU for independent batch latch state, release, reset, contact gating, two-stage forces and dissipative friction/damping. Isaac Lab is not installed, so no USD import, contact sensor hookup, PhysX simulation or cross-engine trajectory matching is claimed.

## Acceptance scope, execution and remaining calibration

`tests/test_mechanisms.py` drives forces through `xfrc_applied`, with torque r×F about each body's world COM to apply the force at the edge/button/rim site. It does not drive joint position targets. The opening and closing cycle, latched hold, free hinge and pad pull-off, button ramp/return, continuous table rotation, energy decay and timestep convergence are force tests. The static collision grid is a separate geometric supplement. Every dynamic step checks finite state/energy and monitors contacts; each test rejects >2 mm penetration or MuJoCo warnings. Energy assertions are taken after the external push, not while energy is deliberately injected. Failure to open is not hidden by an angle assignment.

The exact run results and timings appear below and in `tests/results.json`; raw traces with units are in `tests/traces.json`. Tests establish internal consistency with **assumed** acceptance bands, not successful sim-to-real transfer. Missing hardware inputs: exact model label, exterior depth and tray diameter, empty mass and separate door mass, button force/travel curve, free hinge breakaway and damping, opening trajectory, maximum stop angle, and actual latch geometry. These are the next calibration measurements; no unsupported performance tolerance is asserted.

`review.jpg` contains rest, 50° half-open, 100° full-open, and button/hook detail, plus actual force/travel and pop-angle plots. Blender poses are explicitly illustrative, not dynamic replay or source reconstructions. The work uses existing captures; no new capture is created, so no new camera reconstruction/replay is asserted. Deliverables are in the user-requested mechanism directory rather than a new test-scene directory. No personal-site publication is part of this mechanism delivery.
